DISCOVERY

F001
SEVERITY: 0.98
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually run tests against the patched source tree. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it writes only the patched target file into a temp directory as `tmpdir/<basename>.py`, but then executes the caller-provided `test_cmd` unchanged with `cwd=tmpdir`. The default integration path in `immune_agents.py` passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which resolves relative to the tempdir and therefore targets a non-existent `bench/tests/` subtree. Even when a custom test command exists, it still points at original paths unless manually rewritten. Evidence in code: patched file is created in isolation, no project tree is copied, no import path is redirected, and `test_cmd` is forwarded verbatim.
FOLLOW: This breaks the core “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature on the happy path. Fixes can be marked HARMFUL because tests fail due to missing paths, not due to the patch. More dangerous, fixes can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL without exercising real imports if no meaningful tests run. That misleads the immune pipeline’s Stage 4 verification, which sets `finding.verified = True` for SAFE/NEUTRAL results; downstream NK bug-closed logic then suppresses future findings for a bug that was never actually validated in a representative sandbox.
PROPOSED_FIX: Build a minimal sandbox project tree instead of a single-file temp copy: copy the repository subtree needed for `source_paths` and tests into `tmpdir`, apply the patch at its relative path, and run `test_cmd` against that copied tree from the sandbox root.
VERIFIED: TRUE

F002
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` measures pre-fix and post-fix diagnostics on different analysis scopes, so the net comparison is mechanically unsound. Pre-fix counts are gathered by running tools on the original file in its real project location. Post-fix counts are gathered by running the same tools on a standalone temp file containing only that one file. Type checkers and linters that depend on project context, config files, package layout, sibling modules, or imports will produce different results for reasons unrelated to the patch. Evidence: `pre_* = _count_tool_issues(..., target_path)` uses real path; patched file is written as `tmpdir/<basename>` with no surrounding package/config copied; `run_pyright/run_mypy/run_ruff/run_bandit` are then run on that isolated file.
FOLLOW: The verdict engine can classify harmful fixes as SAFE when isolation suppresses project-context errors, and classify safe fixes as HARMFUL when isolation introduces spurious import/config failures. This directly corrupts Stage 4 fix verification, causing false `verified=True` promotion or false rejection. Because verified fixes feed NK’s bug-closed gate across rounds, the error propagates into canonical bug lifecycle management, not just a local report.
PROPOSED_FIX: Run both baseline and patched analyses inside the same sandboxed copied project tree, with identical tool invocation context before and after applying the patch, so only the patch changes between measurements.
VERIFIED: TRUE

F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong source file when multiple `source_paths` share a suffix or when a finding mentions a short filename. It matches by `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`, then returns the first match. A mention like `endocrine.py` or `brain.py` is ambiguous across directories, and substring matching (`match in sp_path`) can also spuriously match unrelated paths. Evidence: no exact canonical path resolution, no ambiguity detection, first-match return.
FOLLOW: Wrong-file targeting makes fix evaluation report on a different file than the finding refers to. The patch may apply cleanly to the wrong file, yielding bogus SAFE/NEUTRAL/HARMFUL verdicts. That contaminates immune Stage 4 verification and can close or reject bugs unrelated to the proposed fix. Because the module reports `original_file`, this also misleads human review.
PROPOSED_FIX: Resolve only exact basename-or-relative-path matches against `source_paths`; if multiple candidates match, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing.
VERIFIED: TRUE

F004
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: FIND — whole-file fix application can silently replace the wrong module content because `_apply_fix_to_source()` treats any syntactically valid Python snippet with at least 5 newline characters as a complete file replacement, without checking that it is intended for the target file or related to the original content. Evidence: after `compile(fix, "<fix>", "exec")`, the function returns `fix` solely on line-count threshold.
FOLLOW: A prose-heavy or cross-file proposed fix that happens to parse as Python can overwrite the sandbox file with unrelated code. Subsequent tool runs then evaluate an arbitrary replacement, not the proposed root-cause change. That yields misleading SAFE/HARMFUL results and can incorrectly set `verified=True`, poisoning downstream bug-closure decisions. The issue is high for this PoC because models often emit multi-line code blocks that are not full-file replacements.
PROPOSED_FIX: Only allow whole-file replacement when the proposed fix explicitly identifies itself as a full file body for the target file; otherwise skip this strategy and require a search/replace or line-targeted patch.
VERIFIED: TRUE

VERDICT

EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` not only misreports missing tools as available; the same pattern also misreports timed-out tools as available because runners return `[]` on `_run_tool(...).stderr == "TIMEOUT"` via parse failure or empty-output path. This makes the health scan look clean precisely when tooling failed, degrading the brain’s health signal.

EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is also load-bearing inside fix evaluation. `_count_tool_issues()` converts timed-out tool runs into `0`, so a timeout during post-fix analysis can make a patch appear to reduce errors and therefore look SAFE. This is not limited to health scan visibility; it corrupts the SAFE/HARMFUL verdict path.

CONFIRM C0005

EXTEND C0005 | The dead/partial feature surface includes the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” guarantee. Current implementation does sandbox writes, but not sandboxed project-context analysis or testing, so the feature fires with misleading semantics rather than true validation.

CONFIRM C0029
